hints.title: Catalan Root Choice Obstacle
hints.text: Every number from 1 to n can serve as the root node of an ordered search tree. For a chosen root i, how does the number of smaller keys and larger keys determine the count of distinct trees?

hints.title: Cartesian Product Invariant
hints.text: If key i is the root, keys 1 to i - 1 form the left subtree (size i - 1) and keys i + 1 to n form the right subtree (size n - i). The combinations multiply independently.

hints.title: Iterative Catalan Tabulation Procedure
hints.text: Initialize an array dp of size n + 1 with dp[0] = dp[1] = 1. For each length len from 2 to n, compute dp[len] as the sum of dp[i - 1] * dp[len - i] for each root i from 1 to len. Return dp[n].

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Iterative Catalan number tabulation filling an array of size n + 1 in quadratic operations.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating all structural trees recursively without tabulation computes overlapping subproblems in exponential Catalan time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(N) memory for the dynamic programming table.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognizing that structural combinations depend only on subtree sizes, not actual node values.
